description: A social adult day program where older adults spend the day with supervision, activities, and company. It can also give family caregivers a break.

address: 1150 Webster Ave, 2nd Floor, Suite 1, Bronx, NY 10456

description: A social adult day program where older adults spend the day with supervision, activities, and company. It can also give family caregivers a break.

name: The William A. Tieck ADAP Program
organization: The William A. Tieck ADAP Program
description: A social adult day program where older adults spend the day with supervision, activities, and company. It can also give family caregivers a break.

name: PSS Caregiver Hotline
description: A free toll-free hotline from Presbyterian Senior Services for people caring for an older loved one. You can call or text.

name: PSS Dementia Caregivers Program
description: Support from Presbyterian Senior Services for people caring for someone with dementia. Call to learn more.

name: PSS Kinship Caregivers Program (grandparents raising children)
description: Support from Presbyterian Senior Services for older relatives, such as grandparents, who are raising children. Call to learn more.

name: PSS Case Management Program
description: Social workers help older adults with unmet needs. Services include home-delivered meals, NYC Aging-funded home care, referrals, mental health and emotional well-being resources, and help with benefits and entitlements.
eligibility: Age 60 or older, homebound, and living in Bronx Community District 9, 10, or 11.

name: R.A.I.N. Home Attendant Services, Inc.
description: Home attendant services from R.A.I.N. for people who need help at home. Call to ask about eligibility and services.

name: The Hebrew Home at Riverdale
description: Provides around-the-clock skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and help with daily activities for older adults who need ongoing care. The campus also offers memory care and other medical and social supports.
eligibility: For older adults who need daily assistance or more comprehensive care; specific admission requirements are unknown.

name: CenterLight PACE – Wallerstein Center
description: PACE centers provide primary care, social services, physical and occupational therapy, personal care and supportive services, nutrition services and counseling, recreational therapy, and meals.
eligibility: PACE participants; the centers serve residents of the Bronx.

name: In-Home Services / Case Management
organization: NYC Department for the Aging (NYC Aging)
description: A local case manager can assess your needs during an in-home visit and help coordinate services, including meals, home care, and community resources.
eligibility: Residents ages 60 and older; a case manager determines eligibility.
cost: Case management is free. Depending on income, some services may have a fee or suggested contribution. NYC Aging-funded home care is not available to Medicaid recipients.

name: NYC Aging Caregiver Support
description: NYC Aging connects caregivers with information, counseling, support groups, training, respite care, and other help. Call Aging Connect to find programs near you.
eligibility: For people caring for a loved one who needs support; further eligibility details are unknown.

name: Home Care Services Program (HCSP)
description: Get care at home instead of moving into a nursing home. Depending on your needs, care may include a home nurse, house cleaning, or physical therapy.
eligibility: Must be eligible for Medicaid; programs have different eligibility requirements.

name: CaringKind Helpline and Dementia Consultation
description: Call or contact CaringKind online or by email for information, education, emotional support, and guidance about dementia and available programs.
eligibility: For people and families affected by dementia; no other eligibility details stated.
cost: CaringKind says its programs and services are free.

name: VNS Health Home Care
description: VNS Health provides care at home, including help after a hospital stay and support to stay safe and healthy at home. Services are available in the Bronx.
eligibility: For people who need care after a hospital stay or help staying safe and healthy at home.

name: NY Connects: Your Link to Long Term Services and Supports
organization: New York State Office for the Aging (NYSOFA)
description: NY Connects helps people find information about services and supports that can help them live at home and in the community. It can also help people explore eligibility and apply for public benefits.
eligibility: People of all ages or with any type of disability; services are linked regardless of payment source or health insurance.

name: Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
organization: Office of the State Long Term Care Ombudsman
description: The program advocates for people living in long-term care facilities. Regional Ombudsman programs serve communities throughout New York State.
eligibility: People living in long-term care facilities

name: Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program (CDPAP)
organization: New York State Department of Health
description: CDPAP lets eligible Medicaid members choose and train a caregiver to help them at home. The caregiver may be a friend or family member, with some exceptions.
eligibility: Must be eligible for NYS Medicaid, have a stable medical condition and a determined need for home-care services, and be able to self-direct or have a designated representative.

name: Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline
description: Call to speak with staff for information, local resources, crisis assistance and emotional support related to dementia. Staff can also help with care planning and finding programs and services.
eligibility: Anyone can contact the helpline, including people living with dementia, caregivers, families and the public.
hours: Available around the clock, 365 days a year.

name: BronxWorks Minor Repair Program
description: A technician makes minor home repairs and performs security checks to help seniors stay safe at home. The program can also arrange for a technician to change a smoke detector battery.
eligibility: Seniors; other eligibility requirements are unknown.

name: BronxWorks Seniors Homelessness Prevention Project
description: This program helps eligible residents avoid eviction when they have an active case against them in Bronx Housing Court.
eligibility: Low-income Bronx residents aged 60 years or older with an active case against them in Bronx Housing Court.

name: BronxWorks Senior Housing Assistance Program
description: A housing specialist can help seniors fill out housing applications, provide tenant-landlord advocacy, and apply for SCRIE or DRIE. The specialist can also provide information about housing rights and lists of senior housing complexes; BronxWorks does not rent apartments.

name: NYCHA Public Housing
description: NYCHA offers affordable rental housing, with rent based on your family’s income. Some apartments are designed for people with mobility impairments, and senior public housing is available to eligible households.
eligibility: Household income must be at or below the program's limit, and at least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or have eligible immigration status. Applicants must meet NYCHA’s age and household rules; for senior public housing, everyone in the household must be 62 or older.
cost: Rent is based on family income; utilities are included in most buildings.

name: Disabled Homeowners’ Exemption (DHE)
description: DHE can lower property taxes for eligible homeowners with disabilities by reducing the home’s assessed value. Apply by March 15; benefits begin July 1 of that year.
eligibility: Own and live in a one-, two-, or three-family home, condo, or co-op as your primary residence. Owners must meet the disability rules set by the program, and combined owner income must be $58,399 or less. Available to eligible NYC homeowners.

name: Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE)
description: DRIE can keep your rent at the same amount even if your landlord raises it. Eligible tenants must renew each year.
eligibility: Age 18 or older; name on the lease; household income of $50,000 or less per year; spend more than one-third of monthly income on rent; live in an eligible rent-regulated apartment or other eligible housing; receive a qualifying disability benefit. No immigration-status requirement is stated.

name: Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE)
description: SCRIE can freeze an eligible senior tenant’s rent at its current level and protect them from future rent increases. Tenants must submit a renewal application to continue receiving benefits.
eligibility: Eligible senior citizen tenants; further criteria are not stated.

name: Senior Citizen Homeowners’ Exemption (SCHE)
organization: New York City Department of Finance
description: SCHE can reduce the assessed value of an eligible homeowner’s home for property tax purposes. Eligible homeowners can apply or renew online or by mailing a paper application.
eligibility: All owners must be 65 or older, unless the co-owners are spouses or siblings, in which case only one must be 65 or older. Combined annual income must not exceed $58,399. The owner must generally have owned the property for at least 12 consecutive months and all owners must occupy it as their primary residence, subject to stated exceptions.

name: Tenant Helpline
description: Get information about tenant rights and help finding housing-related resources. Specialists can also connect tenants to services such as free legal help and mediation.
eligibility: Available to all New Yorkers, regardless of immigration status.

name: Housing Court Answers
description: A free phone hotline for tenants with questions about eviction cases, Housing Court, or serious apartment repairs. It is open on weekdays.
eligibility: Tenants with housing or eviction questions

name: HomeFix Program
organization: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD), in partnership with Center for NYC Neighborhoods (CNYCN) and Restored Homes Housing Development Fund Corporation
description: HomeFix offers loans for eligible homeowners to make repairs to their homes. It also provides help with applications, contractors, construction oversight, financial counseling, and other homeowner needs.
eligibility: Owners of one- to four-family homes in any NYC borough, including the Bronx, who live in the home as their primary residence 270 days per year; do not own another property within 100 miles of NYC; have no reverse mortgage; and have household income at or below 120% AMI. Condos and co-ops are not eligible.
cost: Affordable low- or no-interest loans that may be forgivable; terms may also be fully amortizing at 0–5% interest. Loans are up to $100,000 per home, plus $30,000 per additional rental unit. Favorable terms are available for low-income and senior households.

name: Senior Resident Advisor (SRA) & Service Coordinator Programs
description: The program provides on-site assistance to seniors in NYCHA developments. Senior Resident Advisors organize floor captains to check in with other seniors and help avert crises.
eligibility: Seniors living in NYCHA developments citywide; assistance is described for frail, elderly public housing residents.

name: Center for NYC Neighborhoods (CNYCN) homeowner resources
organization: Center for New York City Neighborhoods (CNYCN), NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
description: Homeowners can get free help with foreclosure prevention, flood protection, scam prevention, home maintenance, and estate planning. Help is available by phone or through the Homeowner Hub online.
eligibility: Homeowners; no age requirement is stated.

name: STAR (Basic STAR and Enhanced STAR)
description: STAR provides either a check or direct deposit to help pay school taxes, or a reduction on a school tax bill. Enhanced STAR offers an increased benefit to eligible older homeowners.
eligibility: Eligible homeowners must own the property and use it as their primary residence. Basic STAR has no age restriction; Enhanced STAR generally requires a resident owner to be at least 65 and meet the income limit.

name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP)
organization: NYC Human Resources Administration (HRA), NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: HEAP helps cover heating and cooling costs and can help prevent utility shutoffs. Payments go directly to your utility company or energy provider.
eligibility: Income eligibility is stated for some benefits; other eligibility details are unknown.

name: Heating Equipment Repair & Replacement (HERR) Benefit
organization: NYC Human Resources Administration (HRA), NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: Helps income-eligible homeowners repair or replace a broken furnace, boiler, or other heating equipment.

name: Clean and Tune Benefit
organization: NYC Human Resources Administration (HRA), NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: Income-eligible homeowners can get one heating tune-up to prepare for winter. It may include minor repairs, chimney cleaning, or installation of carbon monoxide detectors or programmable thermostats.

name: Life-sustaining equipment customer registration
description: If you use electric medical equipment at home to stay alive or healthy, you can ask Con Edison to register you so they can contact you in an emergency.
eligibility: Con Edison customers who rely on electric-powered life-sustaining medical equipment; the utility determines whether the equipment qualifies.

name: Home Water Assistance Program
description: Eligible homeowners automatically receive a credit on their water and sewer account. No enrollment is required.
eligibility: New York City homeowners with a one- to four-family home who received a HEAP Regular Heating Benefit for the 2025–2026 heating season, had an approved SCHE or DHE as of March 2026, or had an approved Veteran’s Exemption for 2026.
cost: The program applies credits totaling $191.00 to the water and sewer account.

name: Con Edison Energy Affordability Program
description: Provides monthly energy-bill discounts to eligible Con Edison customers who receive certain government benefits. Some customers are enrolled automatically; others can apply online or send an application and supporting documents.
eligibility: Con Edison customers receiving qualifying government assistance, including HEAP, Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, and other qualifying programs. Eligibility and discount tier depend on the benefit received.
cost: Monthly bill discounts vary by utility service and tier. Discounts range from $3 to $189.83, effective February 1, 2026.

name: Emergency HEAP Benefit
organization: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: This benefit may help if your heat or heating-related electricity is shut off or at risk of being shut off, or if you are running out of heating fuel. For an emergency, contact your HEAP Local District Contact.
eligibility: Income, available resources, and the type of emergency are considered. The household must meet the stated income or benefit-program criteria, have the heating or electric bill in a household member's name, and have resources below the applicable limit; the higher limit applies if a member is age 60 or older or under age 6.
cost: Benefit amounts range from $185 to $900, depending on the type of emergency.

name: HEAP Cooling Assistance Benefit
organization: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: When the benefit is open, eligible households can get a free air conditioner or fan to help keep their home cool.
eligibility: Income or qualifying SNAP, Temporary Assistance, or Code A SSI status may qualify. Other routes and requirements include having a household member age 60 or older or under age 6, meeting the stated citizenship and living-situation rules, and not having a working air conditioner or having one that is at least five years old; additional criteria apply.
cost: One air conditioner or fan per applicant household, not to exceed $800 with installation, or $1,000 for an existing wall-sleeve unit. No additional HEAP cash benefits are available.

name: Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
organization: New York State Homes and Community Renewal
description: The program helps eligible households lower energy bills and improve home safety and comfort. Services are based on an energy audit and may include insulation, heating repairs, and sealing drafts.
eligibility: Household income at or below 60% of the state median income; households receiving HEAP or certain other public benefits may be automatically eligible. Priority is given to seniors, families with children, and people with disabilities. Homeowners and renters may apply.
cost: No cost for homeowners and renters; owners of rental buildings must contribute to improvement costs.

name: Lifeline
organization: Federal Communications Commission (FCC); administered by the Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC)
description: Lifeline helps make phone and internet service more affordable. Eligible subscribers can get a monthly discount on qualifying service from participating providers.
eligibility: Household income at or below 135% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, or participation in certain federal assistance programs, including SNAP, Medicaid, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Supplemental Security Income, Veterans and Survivors Pension Benefits, or certain Tribal Programs.
cost: Eligible subscribers may receive a discount of up to $9.25 per month for qualifying broadband or bundled service, or up to $5.25 per month for voice-only service.

name: BronxWorks Free Tax Help
description: BronxWorks offers a free tax assistance program during tax preparation season.
hours: January through April during tax preparation season.

name: BronxWorks Benefits Access and Assistance
description: The program can screen people for government benefits they may qualify for and help them apply.

name: BJCC Social Services
description: Staff help Bronx residents with benefits like SNAP (food stamps), Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, and SSI, plus eviction prevention and emergency help.
eligibility: Bronx residents; specific eligibility varies by service and is unknown.

name: Catholic Charities South Bronx Center
description: A one-stop center where people can find services and information and resolve problems with experts.

name: HRA Benefits Access Center Crotona
description: A city office where you can apply for and get help with benefits like Cash Assistance and SNAP.

name: HRA Benefits Access Center Rider
description: A city office where you can apply for and get help with benefits like Cash Assistance and SNAP.

name: ACCESS NYC Portal
description: Use this online tool to screen for and apply for public benefits.

name: NYC Free Tax Prep
organization: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
description: Get free help filing your taxes in person, online, or over the phone. The program has Volunteer Income Tax Assistance and Tax Counseling for the Elderly locations across New York City.
eligibility: For tax year 2025, live or work in NYC and earn $97,000 or less with qualifying children or dependents, or $68,000 or less without them.

name: NYC Financial Empowerment Centers
organization: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
description: Get free one-on-one financial counseling in person or by phone. A counselor can help you manage money, improve credit, make a budget, and plan how to handle debt.
eligibility: Age 18 or older and live or work in NYC.

name: Cash Assistance
description: Provides cash help to families in need. Funds are often provided on a debit card, though some families may qualify for payments directly to their landlord.
eligibility: Eligibility depends on income, benefits, household size, and resources. People should apply regardless of immigration status. Applicants age 60 or older are waived from the work, education, or training requirement.

name: LiveOn NY Benefits Outreach
description: Helps older New Yorkers access public benefits, including assistance with applications and renewals. The program also offers outreach events, referrals, and benefits education.
eligibility: For older New Yorkers; specific eligibility requirements are unknown.

name: MyBenefits
description: Use MyBenefits to check eligibility for benefits and apply for food assistance.

name: Free credit report
description: You can request a free copy of your credit report each year through the website or by phone. Review it for accounts or inquiries you do not recognize.

name: Retirement benefits
description: You may receive monthly retirement benefits if you have worked and paid Social Security taxes. You can usually apply starting at age 62, including while still working.
eligibility: Typically available starting at age 62 if you have worked and paid Social Security taxes for 10 years or more.

name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
description: SSI provides monthly payments to older adults and people with disabilities who have little or no income or resources. The amount depends on income, living situation, and other factors.
eligibility: Adults age 65 or older may be eligible if they have little or no income and little or no resources.

name: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
description: Provides monthly payments to people whose disability stops or limits their ability to work. Benefits may also include Medicare.
eligibility: A disability or blindness and enough work history.

name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide
description: IRS-certified volunteers can prepare and file your taxes or coach you so you can prepare them yourself. Find a nearby location using the service locator.
eligibility: For people who qualify, with a special focus on taxpayers over 50 with low to moderate income. AARP membership is not required.

name: RAIN Eastchester Individual Rides for Older Adults (North Bronx)
organization: Regional Aid for Interim Needs Inc
description: Rides for older adults to places like medical appointments, shopping, and older adult centers, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask if you live in their service area.
eligibility: Adults age 60 and older in the program's service area

name: Mid-Bronx Individual Rides for Older Adults (South Bronx)
organization: Mid Bronx Senior Citizens Council Inc
description: Rides for older adults to places like medical appointments, shopping, and older adult centers, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask if you live in their service area.
eligibility: Adults age 60 and older in the program's service area

name: RAIN Eastchester Group Rides for Older Adults (North Bronx)
organization: Regional Aid for Interim Needs Inc
description: Rides for older adults to places like medical appointments, shopping, and older adult centers, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask if you live in their service area.
eligibility: Adults age 60 and older in the program's service area

name: FEJOST Group Rides for Older Adults
description: Rides for older adults to places like medical appointments, shopping, and older adult centers, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask if you live in their service area.
eligibility: Adults age 60 and older in the program's service area

name: Riverdale Y New Beginnings Van Transportation
description: An accessible van provides door-to-door transportation. Call to reserve and leave your name, pick-up address, and phone number.
eligibility: New Beginnings members; membership is for NYC residents age 60+.
hours: Call before 8:00 a.m. to reserve. Return trips leave the Y at 1:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m.; a 3:00 p.m. trip may be available by request.

name: Transportation
description: Transportation is available for essential medical and social service appointments if you lack access to transportation or cannot use public transportation. Group trips may also be available for outings, shopping, and trips to older adult centers.
eligibility: Residents age 60 and older who lack access to transportation or cannot use public transportation; group outing trips require at least five older adults.

name: Fair Fares NYC (FFNYC)
description: Fair Fares NYC gives eligible New Yorkers 50% off subway fares, eligible bus fares, and Access-A-Ride paratransit trips. You can apply online or in person.
eligibility: Must live in NYC, be 18–64 years old, and have household income at or below the program's limit. Available regardless of immigration status.
cost: 50% off eligible fares and Access-A-Ride trips.

name: MTA Reduced-Fare Program (OMNY)
description: Reduced-Fare OMNY customers can contact OMNY Customer Service with questions about payments and transactions.
eligibility: Reduced-Fare OMNY customers; the Reduced-Fare program is available to people 65 or older or people with a qualifying disability.

name: Access-A-Ride (AAR) Paratransit Service
description: Shared-ride transportation for people with disabilities who cannot use buses or subways. It runs 24 hours a day.
eligibility: For eligible customers with disabilities that prevent them from using public buses and subways.
hours: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays.

name: Legal Services NYC – Bronx (Legal Help for Older Adults)
description: Free legal help for older adults in the Bronx, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask if they can help with your legal problem.

name: BronxWorks Elder Abuse Help
description: BronxWorks assists older adults experiencing physical, emotional, verbal, or financial abuse. Help can include restraining orders and referrals to legal counsel, police, the Bronx District Attorney’s office, and Adult Protective Services.

name: Legal Aid Society – Bronx Neighborhood Office
description: The Legal Aid Society lists this as a Bronx office. The organization says it serves clients throughout the five boroughs.

name: Bronx Defenders – Right to Counsel in Housing Court
description: The Bronx Defenders gives free legal help to Bronx tenants facing eviction in Housing Court.
eligibility: People facing eviction or other penalties in housing court

name: Bronx Defenders – Access to Public Benefits
description: The organization provides community members with access to and information about nutritional benefits, transportation benefits, childcare, and healthcare.

name: Mobilization for Justice Bronx office
description: Mobilization for Justice provides free, direct civil legal assistance. It also provides community education, builds partnerships, and engages in policy advocacy and impact litigation.
eligibility: The organization prioritizes people who are low-income, disenfranchised, or have disabilities.

name: Bronx County District Attorney's Office
organization: The Office of the Bronx County District Attorney
description: The office that prosecutes crimes in the Bronx. You can contact it if you or someone you know was the victim of a crime, including scams or abuse.

name: Elder Justice Programs
organization: NYC Aging and community-based Elder Justice programs
description: These programs support older adults affected by elder abuse. Help may include safety planning, counseling, shelter referrals, assessments, and help with court systems.
eligibility: People over age 60 affected by elder abuse; programs are available in each borough.

name: Legal Assistance to Older New Yorkers
description: Provides legal advice, referrals, help with public benefits, and representation in some legal matters. Services can support older adults who are homebound, institutionalized, homeless, or facing abuse, neglect, exploitation, health problems, or language barriers.
eligibility: NYC residents aged 60 years and older
languages: whatever language the client needs or prefers

name: Adult Protective Services (APS)
description: APS helps adults who are at risk of abuse, neglect, or financial exploitation and cannot meet their basic needs. Caseworkers can assess needs, help with benefits, and connect people with other support.
eligibility: Adults 18 or older with a physical or mental disability who cannot manage resources, carry out daily activities, or protect themselves without help, and have no one else able and willing to help responsibly.

name: Right-to-Counsel (Universal Access) legal services for tenants facing eviction
organization: NYC Human Resources Administration (HRA) / Office of Civil Justice (OCJ)
description: If you are facing eviction in Housing Court or a NYCHA administrative proceeding, you can get free legal representation or advice. At your first court appearance, ask for an attorney.
eligibility: Tenants facing eviction in Housing Court or NYCHA administrative proceedings; available in every ZIP code regardless of immigration status.

name: Age discrimination complaint filing
description: Contact the Commission if you believe you experienced unlawful age discrimination at work in New York City. You can file a complaint with its Law Enforcement Bureau.
eligibility: People who believe they experienced unlawful discrimination based on actual or perceived age; employment protections apply to employees, freelancers, independent contractors, and interns, whether paid or unpaid.

name: NYLAG Advance Planning
description: Provides legal advice and help with wills, powers of attorney, health care proxies, and other plans for the future. The team also advises on probate and guardianship options and helps seniors and families address grievances with care providers.
eligibility: New Yorkers with limited means; life-planning documents are prepared for people over 18.

name: VOLS Senior Law Project
description: The project helps older adults prepare life-planning documents, including wills, powers of attorney, and health care proxies. It also offers legal clinics and support related to guardianship, benefits, and planning for burial and funeral expenses.
cost: Life-planning documents are provided free of charge.

name: Elder Abuse Prevention and Interventions — NYS Adult Protective Services Helpline
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Call if you suspect that an older person is being abused. The helpline can help connect you with support.
eligibility: Anyone with concerns about abuse of an adult age 60 or older
hours: 8:30 a.m. to 8 p.m., Monday through Friday

name: New York State Division of Consumer Protection
organization: New York State Division of Consumer Protection
description: Get help related to scams and fraud, and consumer prevention information. The supplied text does not provide contact details.

name: Medicaid Fraud Control Unit (MFCU)
description: The unit investigates Medicaid fraud and abuse or neglect in residential care facilities, hospitals, and clinics. Its New York City Patient Protection Section handles cases in the five boroughs, including the Bronx.

name: JASA Geriatric Mental Health Services – Bronx
organization: The Jewish Association for Services for the Aged
description: Mental health support and counseling for older adults, funded by NYC Aging. Call to ask about services near you.

name: Montefiore Wakefield Mental Health Clinic
description: A Montefiore mental health clinic where you can get counseling and treatment.

name: Montefiore Behavioral Health Center (MBHC), Washington Avenue
description: A Montefiore behavioral health center offering mental health care.

name: Geriatric Mental Health Initiative
description: Licensed clinicians provide mental health screenings, counseling, education, and information and referrals. Services can be in person, virtually, or by phone.
eligibility: Older New Yorkers ages 60 and older; older adult center membership is not required.

name: NYC 988
organization: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
description: Talk, text, or chat with a counselor for mental health or substance use help. Counselors can also provide crisis support, peer support, and referrals to other services.
eligibility: NYC 988 doesn’t ask about immigration status.

name: Geriatric Mental Health information and program finder
organization: New York State Office of Mental Health
description: Information from New York State about mental health conditions and treatment for older adults, plus a tool to find programs.
eligibility: For older adults in New York State; no minimum age is stated.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Call, text, or chat to connect with a counselor for emotional or mental health support. You do not have to be suicidal to reach out.
eligibility: People in the United States and its territories who need support; you do not have to be suicidal.

name: Disaster Distress Helpline
organization: U.S. Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
description: Provides crisis counseling and support for people experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters. Friends, family members, and disaster recovery workers may also benefit.
eligibility: People affected by a natural or human-caused disaster, their friends and family, and disaster recovery workers.

name: Crime Prevention and Support Services (C-PASS)
description: C-PASS helps older adults affected by crimes such as scams, theft, harassment, and assaults. It can help with safety planning, complaints, referrals, and applications for possible reimbursement of crime-related losses and expenses.

name: NYC Cool Options
description: Find nearby places to cool off in hot weather, including official NYC Cooling Centers when they are open.

name: Notify NYC
organization: New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) and the Department of Information Technology & Telecommunications (DoITT)
description: Notify NYC sends alerts about emergencies and important events in New York City. You can receive notifications by text, email, phone, and other methods.

name: Elderly Safe at Home Program (ESAH)
description: The program offers crime-prevention workshops and information about benefits and other support. It can refer residents to community-based services.
eligibility: Seniors and other physically disabled residents at seven developments in the South Bronx.

name: Ready New York: My Emergency Plan
organization: New York City Emergency Management Department
description: This workbook helps you make an emergency plan, record important health information, choose people who can support you, and plan how to evacuate. Caregivers or first responders can also use it to help you.
eligibility: Designed for New Yorkers with disabilities or access and functional needs.

name: Evacuation transportation assistance
organization: New York City Emergency Management Department
description: During a coastal storm or hurricane evacuation order, you can request transportation help if you are in an evacuation zone and have no other safe way to leave. Depending on your needs, the City may take you to an accessible evacuation center or a hospital outside the evacuation zone.
eligibility: People in an evacuation zone under an evacuation order who need assistance or have no other options to evacuate safely; you do not need to be an Access-A-Ride registrant or a U.S. citizen.

name: Special Medical Needs Shelters
description: These emergency shelters offer basic nursing care and health monitoring for people whose medical needs require more support than a general shelter provides but do not require hospitalization. A family member or adult caregiver should accompany each person seeking shelter.
eligibility: People with medical conditions that are not severe enough to require hospitalization but require care not available at general shelters; admission depends on the person's needs and the shelter's capacity.

name: New York State Office of Victims Services
organization: New York State Office of Victims Services
description: Provides help for crime victims with medical bills, counseling expenses, and lost wages. The supplied text does not provide contact details.

name: New York State Domestic and Sexual Violence Hotline

name: DOROT Advance Care Planning

eligibility: Older adults; specific age requirement unknown

name: HCC Monday Night Legal Clinic
description: Speak with an attorney and get advice about legal issues related to your housing.

name: Manhattan District Attorney's Office Elder Abuse Unit
description: Investigates and prosecutes crimes against older adults in Manhattan, including financial exploitation and physical abuse. Call if you or someone you know is being harmed.

name: City Bar Justice Center Legal Hotline

hours: Monday through Friday from 9am – 5 pm; calls received evenings, weekends or holidays will be responded to on the next business day.

hours: Monday–Thursday 8:30 AM–5:30 PM; Friday 8:30 AM–1:00 PM. Closed daily 1:00 PM–2:00 PM and on national holidays. Online forms available 24/7.
